page: Amazon Web Services g6f.large is a graphics-intensive instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, configured with 2 vCPUs, 1 physical core, 2 threads per core, and 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware profile includes a fractional NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with a 0.125 GPU count providing 3 GB of dedicated VRAM, alongside 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The CPU demonstrates strong single-core performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25 percent, and average single-core Geekbench scores. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the lower percentiles, with Geekbench multi-core and Passmark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10 percent. LLM inference speeds for prompt processing using small 135M and medium 7B models achieve average tier results, though text generation speeds remain weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers entry-level access to GPU-accelerated resources without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. The allocation of a fractional NVIDIA L4 GPU and 3 GB VRAM makes it a resource-dense option for lightweight graphics workloads, basic LLM prompt processing, and development environments. It is best suited for lightweight graphics rendering, small-scale machine learning inference, and general-purpose workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not demand high multi-core CPU throughput or massive memory bandwidth.
